newsitem.title: USA: Tourists, park employees stranded in Calif. park.
newsitem.headline: Tourists, park employees stranded in Calif. park.

text.p: About 2,300 tourists, park workers and their families were stranded in California's Yosemite National Park on Thursday because an overflowing river closed highways, a park spokesman said.
"We're completely shut off right now," spokesman Kendell Thompson said.

Heavy rain pushed the Merced River to flood levels, closing all highways into Yosemite Valley, where the headquarters and accommodation of the northern California park is located, the national park said. That prevented people from leaving or entering the scenic park, about 150 miles (240 km) southeast of San Francisco.
Punishing storms have caused havoc throughout the western United States, bringing floods, mudslides and evacuations.
Thompson said there were about 1,100 tourists in Yosemite Valley and about 1,200 staff and their families. Rooms were available for all the guests and park employees had homes in the valley, he said.
"They are warm and dry. There is enough food. The electricity is still on. Everybody is in good shape," he said.
